title: Prior-month ozone had no clear taxon-count association in matched four-state bird surveys in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested prior-month ozone and recorded bird taxa in California, Oregon, New York, and Pennsylvania in 2005-2019. We joined public bird survey records to EPA daily ozone summaries. We used 1,366 consecutive-year pairs with the same route, observer, and ozone site. We fit separate models in two regions and two periods. We controlled for survey weather, date, time, duration, assistant status, observer experience, and state-year changes. Slopes ranged from -0.75 to +0.72 taxa per 10 ppb higher ozone. All four uncertainty intervals included zero, with or without correction for four tests. Closer monitors and closer survey dates did not resolve a common association. Ozone coverage selected 75-79% of filtered eastern surveys and 43-51% of western surveys. Coverage also selected warmer survey starts. These results do not show that ozone is safe for birds. Exposure error, sample selection, small samples, and unmeasured seasonal weather limit inference. The package includes code, hashes, daily monitor evidence, the exposure panel, model inputs, figures, and offline checks.
